items.title: Start with a shipment exception queue

pages.headline: The order is in ERP. The load is in TMS. The problem is still in someone’s inbox.
pages.body: A supplier changes the date but ERP still shows the old PO. A carrier reports a delay that TMS misses. A receipt never posts to ERP. A customer order needs a price decision. Freight charges lack proof; 3PL rework never reaches the invoice. Each case waits while someone finds the record, secures approval and makes the change. These are the six queues in this guide.
pages.callout: The systems record what happened. The team still has to prove what it means, decide what changes and close the loop.

pages.title: Shipment Exception Resolution
pages.problem: The load missed pickup. The TMS shows an on-time milestone, the carrier says it is running late, and the warehouse says the freight was ready. The customer still expects delivery at 17:00. Before the planner can protect that promise, the coordinator checks the carrier, the appointment and the proof — then tries to establish which update is current.
pages.opportunity: Visibility alone does not resolve an exception. Orcaworks reconciles the TMS milestone, carrier reply, warehouse departure and customer commitment into a current operational picture. The planner approves expedite, reschedule or hold before TMS and customer records change.

pages.title: Supplier Promise & PO Change Resolution
pages.problem: ERP still shows Friday, but the supplier’s reply moves half the PO to Tuesday. The change is buried in an email or partial acknowledgement; sales and planning continue using the old date. The buyer must match the reply to the right PO lines, establish what is actually confirmed and decide whether to accept the split or seek alternate supply.
pages.opportunity: Supplier commitments arrive through emails, acknowledgements and portals. Orcaworks matches replies to PO lines and checks changed dates and quantities against demand. The buyer approves the commitment before ERP updates the affected lines and planning or customer service is alerted.

rightContent.label: of procurement leaders saw supplier collaboration rise sharply in priority over the prior 24 months.

pages.headline: The new supplier date belongs on the PO, not just in an email.

pages.title: Customer Order Intake & Exception Resolution
pages.problem: A customer emails a revised PO with a supplier part number, a case quantity and a price that differs from its contract. The earlier version is already in ERP. A CSR has to recognise the revision, map the customer item to the right SKU and UOM, prevent a duplicate and settle the price or date before a clean order can be accepted.
pages.opportunity: Orcaworks checks customer PO revisions against item masters, agreed prices and existing orders. Clean lines are prepared for ERP; disputed SKUs, UOMs, prices and dates go to the CSR or pricing owner. Measure acceptance time and corrections to track the intake work Orcaworks can influence.

pages.title: ERP–WMS–3PL Inventory & Transaction Reconciliation
pages.problem: WMS confirms a receipt of 120 units; ERP still shows zero. The receiving team says the pallet is in the building, but customer service cannot promise it and finance cannot trust the balance. An inventory analyst must distinguish a stuck interface message from a short receipt, duplicate posting, hold or physical discrepancy before changing any stock record.
pages.opportunity: A mismatch does not automatically mean stock is missing. Orcaworks traces the PO, receipt, WMS movement, 3PL report and ERP message to find the transaction break. The inventory owner approves the fix; physical differences stay on hold until a count or inspection supplies proof.

pages.title: Freight Audit & Dispute Resolution
pages.problem: A carrier bills detention and an extra stop. The audit system flags the amount, but the rate confirmation, appointment change, BOL, POD and carrier email are in different places. AP needs to know whether the charge is contractual and supported — not just that the invoice failed the automatic match.
pages.opportunity: Orcaworks assembles the carrier invoice, contracted rate, audit result, BOL/POD and appointment evidence; requests what is missing and identifies the disputed line. The freight-audit or AP owner decides pay, hold or dispute. An authorised outcome is recorded in the freight-payment/AP system with the proof attached.

pages.title: 3PL Billing Assurance
pages.problem: Value-added services (labeling, kitting, rework, and other customer-specific work) make up roughly 9% of the contract logistics market. They are also the work most likely to fall out of billing. The WMS records pallets moved and storage days, but not the relabeling and weekend rework a customer requested, approved by email, and logged on a service ticket. At month-end, the standard rate-card calculation runs on WMS data alone. The result: work that was performed never reaches the invoice, or it is billed with no evidence behind it.
pages.opportunity: Orcaworks closes that gap before the invoice goes out. It compares WMS events, rate-card terms, service tickets, and account approvals, surfacing missing or unsupported charges. Every nonstandard charge or credit is approved before billing, so each invoice line is complete and backed by evidence.

rightContent.label: of the contract logistics market is value-added work, a segment in its own right alongside warehousing and distribution. Every dollar of it needs to reach the invoice.

pages.headline: Bill the work. Show the proof.

pages.headline: Start with one shipment exception queue.
pages.body: Bring late loads, missing milestones and held PODs from one team. For one first-workflow engagement, establish today’s signal-to-decision time, aged exceptions and status touches per load; test approved recovery and TMS write-back against those baselines. Planners keep authority over expedites and customer promises.
